title: Monodromy for norm-topology continuous coefficients on normal schemes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure] with the topology of the extended $\ell$-adic absolute value. Let $X$ be a nonempty connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] separated Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $\ell$ invertible in every local ring. Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact. Assume that each local ring of $X$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar x)$ be the profinite etale fundamental group [def-galois-fibre-functor]. For $K=\Omega$ or any finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq K\subseteq\Omega$, give $K$ its restricted norm topology and put $R_{K,X}=p_X^*C(-,K)$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and lisse in the finite locally free sense [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module].

There are $K$-linear equivalences $\Phi_K$ between lisse $R_{K,X}$-modules and continuous finite-dimensional $K$-linear representations of $\Pi$. Here a representation is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$ with product norm topology in a basis and a homomorphism $\rho:\Pi\to\operatorname{GL}_K(V)$ whose matrix entries are continuous; arrows are equivariant $K$-linear maps. The equivalences send the regular module to the trivial representation $K$, finite direct sums to finite direct sums, and include dimension zero. They are compatible with each inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ for finite $E$: there is an isomorphism, natural in every lisse $R_{E,X}$-module $L$,
$$\Phi_\Omega\bigl(R_{\Omega,X}\otimes_{R_{E,X}}L\bigr)\cong\Omega\otimes_E\Phi_E(L),$$
where tensor on the left is ordinary internal scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] along the ring map obtained by postcomposition with $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ and pullback [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. The right side has action $g(a\otimes v)=a\otimes\rho(g)v$. In particular the scalar-extended module on the left is lisse. All continuous $\Omega$-valued functions are used; no finite-subextension-valued restriction is imposed.

source.place: Section 7.4, Lemma 7.4.7 and Lemma 7.4.10, pp. 70–71, as monodromy framework. Agent-stated norm-topology coefficient strengthening: Remark 7.4.8 instead uses the colimit topology via Example 7.1.7 and is not an exact source for the Omega case or its scalar comparison.

proof.text: First work at a geometric generic point $\bar\eta$. The Noetherian hypothesis gives the descending-chain condition on closed subsets by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Apply [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components]: the normal scheme has finitely many disjoint clopen integral components. Since $X$ is nonempty and connected it has exactly one, so is integral. Write $k=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$, choose $k^s$, and put $G_k=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$. For $A=K$ or a complete normed field containing it, use [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] to identify the specified pulled-back ring with $U\mapsto C(|U|,A)$. This identification uses all continuous maps. A nonarchimedean field is totally disconnected: two distinct points are separated by complementary clopen balls of radius less than their distance.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: Here is the generic restriction argument, including its use on morphisms. Choose an affine pro-etale covering trivializing two lisse modules $L,M$. On each covering object $U$ a map is a rectangular matrix over $R_A(U)$: its columns are the images of the standard basis maps, by the regular module universal property. The ring bijection of [lem-sfb-normal-generic-continuous-sections] extends each matrix of a generic morphism uniquely from $U_\eta$ to $U$. On affine refinements of each overlap, injectivity of that same ring map makes the extended matrices agree with the transition matrices; the generic compatibility equation is therefore also the global one. Use morphism gluing in [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] on underlying sheaves; addition and scalar linearity hold locally and hence globally. Thus restriction to $\eta$ is fully faithful on lisse modules. If a generic map is invertible, extend its inverse too; uniqueness makes the two composites identities. Also, every nonempty affine trivializing object has nonempty generic fibre (otherwise the ring bijection would identify a nonzero constant $1$ with $0$). By [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates], evaluation at any geometric generic point of this fibre compares its free rank with the dimension of $L$ over $k^s$. Consequently the rank is one fixed integer $n$ on the whole trivializing covering; $n=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: Pull $L|_\eta$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. By [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates] choose a basis of its free rank $n$ module. Its descent isomorphism is a matrix $c\in\operatorname{GL}_n(C(G_k,K))$. Evaluate on $g\in G_k$: $\sigma_L(g)=c(g)$ has continuous entries and the Cech identity gives $\sigma_L(gh)=\sigma_L(g)\sigma_L(h)$ and $\sigma_L(1)=1$. A morphism between two such objects is a constant matrix $B$ over $K$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, with descent equation $B\sigma_L(g)=\sigma_M(g)B$. Conversely these equations suffice for gluing the map, by [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent]. Changing the chosen basis conjugates the matrices, so one obtains a functor to representations, independently of a coordinate presentation up to the basis-change isomorphism. Coefficient extension changes every displayed matrix by the coefficient homomorphism, by the same Cech-coordinate node.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: Set $F=\widehat K$ and let $\iota:K\hookrightarrow F$ be the isometric field map of [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. The nonarchimedean inequality holds on $F$ too, by taking limits in that inequality on the dense subfield $K$. For each $n$, $\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ satisfies the complete-group hypotheses of [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy]. Indeed the subgroups $1+\{B:\max_{ij}|B_{ij}|<r\}$ for $0<r<1$ form a neighborhood basis of $1$; multiplication preserves this bound and the geometric series converges in the complete matrix ring to the inverse. A two-sided Cauchy net of invertible matrices has both its matrices and its inverses Cauchy entrywise: fix a sufficiently late matrix to bound the norms of the tail and its inverses, then multiply the small relative differences by these bounds. Their limits $a,b$ satisfy $ab=ba=1$, proving completeness for the two-sided uniformity. This also covers $n=0$, when the group is trivial.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: Form $L_F=R_{F,X}\otimes_{R_{K,X}}L$ along postcomposition by $\iota$. Locally $R_F\otimes_{R_K}R_K^n\cong R_F^n$ by $a\otimes(b_i)\mapsto(a\iota(b_i))$ with inverse $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i\otimes e_i$; these are identities from the tensor relations. Hence $L_F$ is locally free of rank $n$. Its frame sheaf $P(U)=\operatorname{Isom}_{R_{F,U}}(R_{F,U}^n,L_F|_U)$ is an $F_{\operatorname{GL}_n(F)}$-torsor: in a local basis its sections and action are invertible continuous matrices and matrix multiplication. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy] at $\bar\eta$, with the frame $p$ induced by the generic $K$-basis over $k^s$, to obtain $\tau_L:\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$. By the pointed pullback clause of [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy], the homomorphism of the pullback of $(P,p)$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $\tau_Lq$, where $q:G_k\to\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)$ is induced by $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$. By its field clause it is the descent cocycle of the frame $p$ over $k^s$, and by the coefficient formula of [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates] that cocycle is the entrywise image $\iota\sigma_L$ of the Step 3 cocycle. Hence $\iota\sigma_L=\tau_Lq$.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: The continuous map $q:G_k\to\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)$ is surjective by [lem-dl-a1-normal-scheme-galois-inertia-presentation]. For $h\in\ker q$ the equality $\iota\sigma_L(h)=\tau_L(qh)=1$ and injectivity of $\iota$ give $\sigma_L(h)=1$. It therefore factors uniquely as $\sigma_L=\rho_Lq$ with values in $\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$. This factor is continuous: $G_k$ and $\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)$ are profinite, so the continuous surjection $q$ is a quotient map (images of closed subsets are compact and hence closed in the Hausdorff target); each continuous coordinate of $\sigma_L$ descends through this quotient. For maps, Step 3 and surjectivity of $q$ say exactly that their constant generic matrices intertwine $\rho_L$ and $\rho_M$. Together with Step 2 this proves that $L\mapsto\rho_L$ is $K$-linear and fully faithful. No completion-valued matrix is asserted to lie in $K$ without this surjectivity argument.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: For essential surjectivity take $\rho:\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)\to\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$ continuous and let $H=\rho(\pi_1(X,\bar\eta))$ with its subspace topology. It is a compact Hausdorff topological group, and intersections with the small congruence subgroups of $\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$ give an open-subgroup basis. Thus the compact case of [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy] gives a pointed $F_H$-torsor with monodromy $\rho$ viewed as a map into $H$. On a covering trivializing this torsor, glue the free modules $R_K^n$ using the transition functions $H\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$. The cocycle identity for the torsor is exactly the matrix gluing identity. Effective sheaf descent and morphism gluing in [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] glue the underlying sheaf, addition and $R_K$-action; the module identities hold on the covering and therefore globally. The resulting module is lisse by its local construction. After scalar extension to $F$, its frame torsor is the extension of the $H$-torsor along $H\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$, so naturality of torsor monodromy for this map and for the pointed pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, followed by the field clause of [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy], identifies its completed generic cocycle with $\iota\rho q$. The field-coordinate description and injectivity of $\iota$ then identify its generic cocycle with $\rho q$. The functor of Steps 3–6 therefore sends it to $\rho$, proving essential surjectivity.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: Choose a path between the finite fibre functors at $\bar\eta$ and at the prescribed point $\bar x$ using the first paragraph of [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport]. It gives a topological group isomorphism $c_t:\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Pi$. Transport each $\rho_L$ by $c_t^{-1}$, using the same path for every coefficient field. This gives the required equivalences $\Phi_K$. The generic-coordinate description sends the regular module to the one-dimensional trivial representation and a finite sum to the direct sum, since its descent matrix is respectively $1$ and the block sum of the descent matrices. The zero module corresponds to $K^0$, and the constructions in Steps 3–7 use the unique empty matrices for rank zero. Identities, composition and sums of maps are the corresponding matrix operations, so these are $K$-linear equivalences.

source.place: Agent norm-topology extension of the framework of Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71

proof.text: Finally fix finite $E\subseteq\Omega$ and a lisse $R_{E,X}$-module $L$. On a local free chart its ordinary scalar extension is $R_{\Omega}^n$, by $a\otimes(b_i)\mapsto(ab_i)$ and inverse $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i\otimes e_i$. On an overlap its transition matrix is obtained from that of $L$ by entrywise inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$, because both maps send $a\otimes v$ to $a$ times the image of $v$. Thus it is lisse. On the generic separable-closure chart [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates] gives the canonical vector-space comparison $\Omega\otimes_E V\cong V_\Omega$, and its descent action is $a\otimes v\mapsto a\otimes\sigma_L(g)v$. Factoring through the same surjection $q$ and transporting by the same $c_t$ changes this to $a\otimes v\mapsto a\otimes\rho_L(g)v$, as required. For a morphism with generic matrix $B$ both comparison composites have matrix obtained by including the entries of $B$ in $\Omega$, so the comparison is natural. This proves the scalar-extension isomorphism for the specified postcomposition coefficient map, without replacing all continuous functions by finite-subextension-valued ones.
